newsitem.title: USA: Dlr firmer at US noon, then Seguin spurs higher.
newsitem.headline: Dlr firmer at US noon, then Seguin spurs higher.

text.p: The dollar was firm at midday and dollar/mark jumped again just past noon after French National Assembly speaker Philippe Seguin said he wants a broad-based euro, spurring more short-covering, dealers said.

"It was a trap, the move lower on Sunday night. I've got a feeling we're going to enjoy a short-squeeze here up to 1.7120 and possibly higher," said Alfonso Alejo, manager of corporate foreign exchange at Sakura Bank Ltd.
At midday, dollar/mark was trading at 1.7000/10, up from 1.6975/85 at the open and dollar/yen was at 116.50/60 up from 116.35/45.
But immediately after noon, the dollar hurdled its session high near 1.7015 after Seguin's remarks, to be published on Wednesday in the weekly magazine L'Express, hit the wires.

Seguin -- a leading candidate for prime minister if the center-right wins France's parliamentary election run-off on Sunday -- said there should not be an "apothecary's approach" to entry conditions for the single currency, adding: "The maximum number of countries must participate."
The dollar initially built on overnight gains after a strong reading on U.S. consumer optimism scared off shorts and triggered stop/loss buying above 1.70 marks, dealers said.
On Tuesday, the Conference Board said its index of consumer confidence surged to 127.1, a 28-year high, in May.

"Consumer confidence helped, but overall it's really the fact there was those stops up there and with everybody talking about them it was kind of inevitable they were going to get run," said James Powers, a vice president of corporate foreign exchange at Westdeutsche Landesbank Girozentrale.
The consumer sentiment number followed a revised 118.5 in April and came against forecasts of 118.1 for the May index.
But the greenback's rise was temporarily slowed by simultaneous data showing a 2.4 percent decline in April existing home sales, traders said.
Home sales fell to a 4.06 million unit annual rate from a revised 4.16 million unit pace in March. Forecasts averaged 4.09 million units, annualized.

Early New York trade was calm as the market digested the dollar's advance overseas. Traders reported talk of hedge fund sales near 1.70 marks but interbank shorts were quickly reversed as the dollar surpassed that level.

Earlier on Tuesday, the dollar shook off losses in the aftermath of the first round of the snap French election where voters caught the governing center-right coalition off guard by veering sharply to the left.

The initial reaction to Sunday's vote was to buy marks and sell French francs and dollars on fear the left-wing parties might stonewall on further spending cuts needed to meet deficit targets for European Economic and Monetary Union.
"If Socialists were to win, I think that could undermine the whole process," said John Nelson, foreign exchange trading manager at ABN-AMRO Bank.
